statement: Most of NMB's and CRDB's excess return comes from their funding advantage, not lending margin or fees.
evidence: NOT SUPPORTED: funding is not the main source of the difference in returns; funding (+3.01 pp) ranks behind asset deployment (+5.03 pp, NMB) and balance-sheet leverage TA/E alone (-5.28 pp, CRDB), with tax and the NCI share isolated as separate terms
review_note: Tests the NMB - CRDB gap, not the level of excess return: the deposit franchise still lifts both banks' ROE (chapter 6), but it is not what separates them.

statement: The two banks' excess returns rest on different profit engines.
evidence: SUPPORTED: the banks' profit engines differ (NMB: asset yield, funding, fees; CRDB: leverage)

statement: Excess returns are persistent (λ well above zero) but mean-reverting (λ < 1).
verdict: conditionally supported: mean reversion appears in the break-adjusted estimates but is not established in the full-cycle sample
evidence: CRDB [ar1_break_episode; Chow 2015-18 episode, FY2018 excluded p = 0.06] lambda 0.53 [0.21, 0.795]: supported; NMB [ar1_break_episode; Chow 2015-18 episode, FY2018 excluded p = 0.01] lambda 0.69 [0.48, 0.853]: supported; DCB [ar1_benchmark; no known-date break at 10%] lambda 0.20 [-0.50, 1.000]: inconclusive; MBP [ar1_benchmark; no known-date break at 10%] lambda 1.00 [0.79, 1.000]: inconclusive; MKCB [ar1_benchmark; no known-date break at 10%] lambda 0.33 [-0.36, 1.000]: inconclusive; MCB [ar1_benchmark; no known-date break at 10%] lambda 1.00 [0.73, 1.000]: inconclusive; not estimated: MUCOBA

statement: Long-run rent ER\* is positive for NMB and CRDB and near zero or negative for the smaller panel banks.
evidence: THROUGH-THE-CYCLE ER* (AR(1) benchmark, stress years included; decides the verdict, base case): inconclusive. CRDB ER* n/a (undefined) [n/a (undefined), n/a (undefined)]; NMB ER* n/a (undefined) [n/a (undefined), n/a (undefined)]; DCB ER* -25.3% [-34.4%, -19.0%]; MBP ER* n/a (undefined) [n/a (undefined), n/a (undefined)]; MKCB ER* -9.7% [-26.7%, 8.3%]; MCB ER* n/a (undefined) [n/a (undefined), n/a (undefined)]; NMB/CRDB lower bounds at COE + 200 bp: CRDB n/a (undefined), NMB n/a (undefined)
review_note: Through-the-cycle AR(1) lambda = 1.00 for NMB and CRDB, so ER* is undefined there; the break-adjusted ER* is positive for both (open issue 3).

statement: Persistence is higher for banks with a stronger net deposit franchise.
evidence: Spearman(lambda, mean cost of deposits) = -0.12, exact permutation p = 0.84, 6 banks with >= 3 years of cost of deposits: CRDB lambda 0.53, cost 2.05% (n=16); NMB lambda 0.69, cost 1.55% (n=17); DCB lambda 0.20, cost 7.78% (n=6); MBP lambda 1.00, cost 5.77% (n=8); MKCB lambda 0.33, cost 4.73% (n=5); MCB lambda 1.00, cost 6.71% (n=3)

statement: NMB and CRDB have a lower cost of deposits, lower deposit beta and larger net deposit franchise contribution than the smaller banks.
evidence: cost of deposits (mean, lower is better): supported: NMB 0.0155, CRDB 0.0205; smaller banks' median 0.0624 (n=4); deposit beta on the T-bill (lower is better): inconclusive: fewer than 2 smaller banks with data (n=1); NMB 0.0172, CRDB 0.0213; net deposit franchise, ROE points, central (higher is better): supported: NMB 0.0875, CRDB 0.0991; smaller banks' median -0.2013 (n=3)

statement: Loan growth outrunning deposits raises wholesale funding reliance and compresses margin.
evidence: within-bank slope of the change in wholesale share on (loan growth - deposit growth): +0.012 [-0.008, +0.032], n = 81; of the change in NII / assets: +0.0053 [-0.0164, +0.0269], n = 71

statement: Persistence is higher for banks with a stronger net deposit franchise.
evidence: Spearman(lambda, mean net deposit franchise in ROE points) = +0.60, exact permutation p = 0.35, 5 banks: CRDB lambda 0.53, net franchise 9.9%; NMB lambda 0.69, net franchise 8.7%; DCB lambda 0.20, net franchise -27.8%; MBP lambda 1.00, net franchise -17.0%; MKCB lambda 0.33, net franchise -20.1%

statement: Retained earnings have been reinvested at returns above COE for both banks.
verdict_by_bank: CRDB above COE only in windows ending in the post-2018 recovery (FY2021-2025), so not supported through the cycle; inconclusive overall, NMB supported
evidence: CRDB k=5: raise-adjusted 11 windows, median RORE - COE 1.9%, above COE + 200 bp in 45%, below COE - 200 bp in 45%; primary 6 windows, median 32.8%; excluding stress-start windows -13.2%; CRDB k=3: raise-adjusted 13 windows, median RORE - COE 21.2%, above COE + 200 bp in 69%, below COE - 200 bp in 31%; primary 10 windows, median 24.6%; excluding stress-start windows 21.2%; NMB k=5: raise-adjusted 13 windows, median RORE - COE 8.3%, above COE + 200 bp in 62%, below COE - 200 bp in 31%; primary 13 windows, median 8.3%; excluding stress-start windows 8.3%; NMB k=3: raise-adjusted 15 windows, median RORE - COE 22.0%, above COE + 200 bp in 67%, below COE - 200 bp in 27%; primary 15 windows, median 22.0%; excluding stress-start windows 22.0%; per bank (k = 5): CRDB above COE only in windows ending in the post-2018 recovery (FY2021-2025), so not supported through the cycle; inconclusive overall, NMB supported
review_note: Open issue 4: for CRDB, excluding windows that start in FY2015-18 leaves 7 windows with a raise-adjusted median RORE of 8.6% and a median excess over the window COE of -13.2%; windows clearing COE + 200 bp start in FY2016, FY2017, FY2018, FY2019, FY2020 (ending FY2021-2025). Wording accepted by the owner (2026-11-09): 'supported for NMB; for CRDB above COE only in windows that end in the post-2018 recovery, so not supported through the cycle; inconclusive overall'.

statement: Incremental returns are declining as the banks scale.
evidence: within-bank slope of incremental ROE (k = 3, raise-adjusted RORE) on log average assets: +0.14; 90% moving-block bootstrap interval [-0.07, +0.62] (block 3, 2,000 replicates, windows resampled in blocks within each bank); OLS t interval [-0.06, +0.34] (verdict on the t interval: inconclusive; change: none); n = 28 overlapping windows; per bank: CRDB +0.22, block bootstrap [-0.27, +1.37] (t interval [-0.16, +0.60], n=13); NMB +0.09, block bootstrap [-0.61, +0.85] (t interval [-0.14, +0.32], n=15)

statement: The banks differ in capital allocation (growth versus distribution).
evidence: mean payout 2010-25: NMB 34.0%, CRDB 35.2% (Welch p = 0.37); mean RWA growth: NMB 18.7%, CRDB 19.0% (p = 0.95); mean Tier 1 headroom: NMB 9.7%, CRDB 3.5%

statement: The current low cost of risk is below the through-the-cycle level.
evidence: CRDB FY2025: 1.26% vs TTC 2.00% (FY2010-2025 (16 years)), gap -0.74% [block bootstrap -1.53%, -0.11%; i.i.d. -1.22%, -0.30%]; current below TTC under 100% of cycle definitions; CRDB FY2023-2025 mean: 0.92% vs TTC 2.00% (FY2010-2025 (16 years)), gap -1.08% [block bootstrap -1.87%, -0.45%; i.i.d. -1.56%, -0.63%]; current below TTC under 100% of cycle definitions; NMB FY2025: 0.84% vs TTC 1.84% (FY2010-2025 (16 years)), gap -1.00% [block bootstrap -1.87%, -0.50%; i.i.d. -1.52%, -0.49%]; current below TTC under 100% of cycle definitions; NMB FY2023-2025 mean: 1.03% vs TTC 1.84% (FY2010-2025 (16 years)), gap -0.81% [block bootstrap -1.68%, -0.31%; i.i.d. -1.34%, -0.31%]; current below TTC under 100% of cycle definitions

statement: Return on RWA differs between the banks after adjusting for credit cost.
evidence: NMB - CRDB risk-adjusted RoRWA (pre-tax, own TTC cost of risk), mean over 15 years (FY2010-2025): +3.01% [+2.20%, +3.86%]; unadjusted return on RWA (after tax) +2.01% [+1.25%, +2.65%]
review_note: NMB's RWA is Bank-solo and its profit Group (D2): the gap includes a small basis effect (open issue 5).
